Title: Acta Bosnae potissimum ecclesiastica cum insertis editorum documentorum regestis ab anno 925 usque ad annum 1752 (Monumenta spectantia historiam Slavorum meridionalium, volumen vicesimum tertium)
Creator: Compiled and arranged by P. Eusebius Fermendžin (title page: "Collegit et digessit P. Eusebius Fermendzin"); issued by the Academia scientiarum et artium Slavorum meridionalium (Yugoslav Academy of Sciences and Arts)
Publisher: Zagreb (Zagrabiae): Academia scientiarum et artium Slavorum meridionalium, printed by the Society's press; title page "ZAGRABIAE 1892"
Publication Date: 1892
Rights: Public Domain
Rights basis: pd-us-by-date. The title page of the scan reads "ZAGRABIAE 1892" (file lines 121 and 148); the host item record gives date 1892 and possible-copyright-status NOT_IN_COPYRIGHT.
Language: lat
Source: Internet Archive item actabosnaepotis00fermgoog (archive.org/details/actabosnaepotis00fermgoog), full-text file actabosnaepotis00fermgoog_djvu.txt, fetched directly by the Library thread, October 2026. Contributor named by the host: Harvard University (Harvard College Library, Henry Lillie Pierce stamp).
Provenance note: Header prepended; the host text follows unchanged. Nothing was normalised, stripped, corrected, re-spaced or retyped. The Google Books boilerplate pages at the head are left in place. OCR sampled at 5, 50 and 95 percent: readable medieval Latin in regest form, every word followed by a doubled space and with scattered OCR damage (for example "haereticis" read as "haeretids"); Slavonic and Croatian names and the Croatian footnotes are mixed in.
Content note: A calendar of papal, royal, Ragusan and Franciscan documents on Bosnia from 925 to 1752, with the Latin of the key passages quoted. It is the Roman and outside record of the Bosnian Church, not the church's own voice. Landmarks: Innocent III to King Emeric of Hungary, 11 October 1200, on Ban Kulin who gave the heretics "non modo tutum habitaculum sed et praesidium manifestum" (file line 548); Gregory IX to the bishop of Bosnia, 1234, on preaching against the heretics of Slavonia (757); Innocent IV, 1247, saying the church and diocese of Bosnia have "totaliter lapsa ... in perfidiam hereticae pravitatis" (1086); Boniface VIII, 1303, ordering proceedings "contra haereticos et patarenos, credentes et receptores eorum" (1406); Gregory XI, 1376, licence for a Franciscan house to preach to "scismaticis ac patarenis" (3123); the Ragusan privilege to Radin Gost, November 1455 (14981); Duke Stephen crossing at Novi in March 1453 with his son Vlatko and "gost Radin" (14415); and Duke Stephen's testament of 1466 (the OCR reads the day as "30 Mali"; Truhelka's article gives 21 May), naming "gost Radin, metropolita (in Milešovo) David" among his household as witnesses (17606 to 17608). Gost Radin's testament itself is not in this volume. Second witness for exact wording.
